hook.line: Sometimes you want to give a verdict that sounds thought through, not just blurted out. *Resulta… que* says: after thinking about it, this is how it strikes me.
hook.es: Resulta absurdo que nadie se diera cuenta antes.
hook.en: It's absurd that nobody noticed before.

examples.en: It's absurd that nobody noticed before.

rule:
*Resulta* + adjective is a verdict that follows from reflection. It is a touch more thoughtful than *es*.

Two shapes:
*Resulta* + adjective + *que* + subjunctive, for a reaction: *Resulta raro que Vale no venga*. You are judging the fact, not announcing it, so the verb is subjunctive.
*Resulta* + adjective + infinitive, for something general: *resulta más barato reparar*.

Link with plain *que*, never *de que*.
*De buen / mal gusto* judges whether something is socially fitting, not how well it is made.
Compare *salta a la vista que*, which states a fact and takes the indicative.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an impersonal expression of evaluation. It triggers the subjunctive because it reacts to the fact.

Nobody noticed that it was absurd.

options: In the long run buying works out cheaper than repairing.
In the long run repairing works out cheaper than buying.
In the long run repairing is cheap.

options: I like laughing at that.
I think it's in very good taste to laugh at that.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Resulta vergonzoso que el dueño no ___ perdón.* (*pide* or *pida*) It's shameful that the owner doesn't apologise.
yourTurn.answer: Resulta vergonzoso que el dueño no pida perdón.
yourTurn.why: A verdict on a fact takes the subjunctive, *pida*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *A la larga resulta más barato ___ que comprar.* (*reparar* or *repara*) In the long run it works out cheaper to repair than to buy.
yourTurn.answer: A la larga resulta más barato reparar que comprar.
yourTurn.why: For something general, use the infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's strange that Vale isn't coming today.
yourTurn.answer: Resulta raro que Vale no venga hoy.
yourTurn.why: After *resulta raro que*, the verb is subjunctive: *venga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I think it's in very bad taste to laugh at that.
yourTurn.answer: Me parece de muy mal gusto reírse de eso.
yourTurn.why: *De muy mal gusto* judges whether something is socially fitting.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's incredible that so many people applaud that.
yourTurn.answer: Resulta increíble que tanta gente aplauda eso.
yourTurn.why: Singular *gente* takes singular *aplauda*, in the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it positive: *Resulta raro que Vale no venga hoy.*
yourTurn.answer: Resulta raro que Vale venga hoy.
yourTurn.why: Take out the *no* and the subjunctive stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: In the long run it works out cheaper to repair.
yourTurn.answer: A la larga resulta más barato reparar.
accept: Resulta más barato reparar a la larga.
yourTurn.why: *A la larga* means "in the long run".

pitfalls.wrong: Resulta absurdo que nadie se dio cuenta antes.
pitfalls.right: Resulta absurdo que nadie se diera cuenta antes.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are judging the fact, not just reporting it, so the verb is subjunctive.

pitfalls.wrong: Resulta raro de que Vale no venga hoy.
pitfalls.right: Resulta raro que Vale no venga hoy.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Spanish links with plain *que*, no *de*.

pitfalls.wrong: A la larga resulta más barato reparar de comprar.
pitfalls.right: A la larga resulta más barato reparar que comprar.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Comparing two things takes *que*, as in "cheaper than".

personal: Say one thing that strikes you as absurd or strange. Use *Resulta… que…*.
